newsitem.title: USA: U.S. farm real estate values rising -- USDA.
newsitem.headline: U.S. farm real estate values rising -- USDA.

text.p: U.S. farm real estate values rose for the ninth year in a row in 1995 and are likely to increase this year, according to a report by the U.S. Agriculture Department's Economic Research Service.
USDA's research arm said its Jan. 1, 1996, valuation of $890 per acre for farmland and buildings marked a seven percent increase and the strongest yearly gain since 1987.

It said with economic conditions favorable in 1996, farm values are likely to increase for the year, supported by improved farm returns and strong domestic and foreign demand for U.S. agricultural products.
